target_customer: Health conscious urban consumers in Colombian cities buying groceries online or from small stores
problem: Healthy and eco friendly groceries were hard to find in one place with fast delivery in Colombia.
business_model: Online and physical grocery retail with private label products and margin on resale

founders.name: Jabib Char
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him an industrial engineer and health educator.

founders.name: Cristina Char
education: Business administration; Master in Management and Master in Visual and Digital Media, IE Business School (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Marketing experience in mass consumption products, retail and non profits per YC page. Crunchbase titles her CMO.

founders.name: Andrés Iriarte
education: BA International Business; BS Management Sciences (per YC page)

founders.name: Alex Ramírez
founders.background_notes: YC page says Mexican software engineer with 15+ years on LATAM tech teams, employers not named.

founders.name: María José Ramos
founders.background_notes: Forbes Colombia (2021-09-30) describes her as a cofounder; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Merqueo
competitors.what: Colombian app delivering supermarket orders from its own warehouses
competitors.traction_then: Led the home grocery delivery segment per La Republica; demand up to four times normal in the pandemic

competitors.name: Rappi
competitors.what: Delivery super app with grocery orders and premium delivery discounts
competitors.traction_then: Reported growth in large basket grocery orders

technical_complexity.rationale: E-commerce and delivery logistics for a small catalog; the difficulty was operations and sourcing, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Private label products and a curated healthy sourcing standard help, but large delivery apps and supermarkets can stock similar items.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A January 2022 article notes new quick commerce entrants such as Jokr and Rappi; no evidence found that they displaced FitHub.

market_need_then: The pandemic pushed Colombian grocery shopping online, and Forbes reported FitHub grew 10x in the year to September 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses fithub.com.co, a Colombian domain, not the .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as a healthy supermarket; Crunchbase says private label builds community around products

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes Colombia listed FitHub in its 30 under 30 coverage in March 2021; no merch or fan content found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press coverage and a founder with a branding role, but the name is generic for fitness products and no distinctive assets were found.

outcome_analysis: FitHub grew about 10x in the year to September 2021, reported more than 2,000 products across eight cities, and raised a US$1.4M seed led by Capital Energy. The online grocery space is capital hungry and crowded with Merqueo, Rappi and quick commerce entrants. No later round or exit was found, so the later trajectory is unknown despite an Active status.
notes: Seed amount is stated by Forbes Colombia and SeedTable. CB Insights lists only $130K total raised, which conflicts. Company website fetch returned only a title (Supermercado Saludable). No outcome news found for FitHub in the search. Founded 2017 per YC page and Forbes 30 under 30 (August 2017).
